PWAY0001.description: This unit provides a comprehensive introduction to university study, helping students build the skills, confidence, and knowledge needed to succeed in higher education. Through a combination of practical activities, guided practice, and reflective learning, students will develop strategies for independent learning, effective study, and time management, enabling them to manage academic tasks with confidence. Students will also gain experience in teamwork, effective communication, and using digital learning tools, preparing them to collaborate effectively and engage fully in the academic environment. The unit encourages students to explore their own learning styles and develop critical thinking skills, providing a strong foundation for future study and academic success.
PWAY0001.outcomes: Students are able to (1) identify the key expectations and skills required for successful university study; (2) communicate effectively in written and oral forms suitable for university contexts; and (3) apply practical study and time management techniques to support independent learning.
PWAY0001.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) discussion board introduction; (2) team poster; and (3) reflection. Further information is available in the unit outline.



This unit is assessed on an ungraded pass/ungraded failed basis. All assessment items must be successfully completed.

Supplementary assessment is not available in this unit.
PWAY0001.contactHours:
This is a preparation unit for the pathway programs. Students have to attend 4 full days. Each day students will attend tutorials, lectures and take part in engaging activities.
Approx hours per day 6 - 7.

PWAY0002.description: This unit develops students' information literacy by supporting the development of skills to recognise when information is needed, determine what is required, locate relevant sources, and critically evaluate and organise that information. It introduces key concepts and practical skills for effectively accessing and using information in academic contexts. Emphasis is placed on navigating major information sources, including libraries, electronic databases, and the Internet. By the end of the unit, students will have the knowledge and skills necessary to undertake university-level research tasks with confidence and competence.
PWAY0002.outcomes: Students are able to (1) analyse a research task by identifying key ideas, questions, and relevant concept; (2) apply strategies to locate and select credible scholarly and authoritative non-scholarly sources; (3) evaluate sources to assess their reliability, usefulness, and relevance of information; and (4) accurately summarise, synthesise, and reference information using appropriate academic conventions and integrity standards.
PWAY0002.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) search strings and research cycle; (2) research presentation; and (3) synthesis. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Supplementary assessment is not available in this unit.
PWAY0002.contactHours:
2h x 14 weeks = 28 hours
8 hours of assessment preparation and self-study = 8 hrs x 14 = 112 hours
Total: 140 hours

PWAY0003.description: This unit focuses on building students' skills in academic writing across various contexts. Students will learn how to effectively integrate research into their writing through techniques such as paraphrasing, quoting, and summarising, while also applying appropriate referencing conventions. Additionally, the unit aims to enhance students' technical writing abilities to support a broad range of academic tasks.
PWAY0003.outcomes: Students are able to (1) apply academic writing conventions to create a variety of text types; (2) construct organised, cohesive, and purposeful paragraphs tailored for a range of purposes; (3) recognise and effectively incorporate paraphrasing, direct quotations, and summarising techniques within written work; and (4) show competence in the stages of the writing process, including planning, research, drafting, revising, and proper referencing.
PWAY0003.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) paraphrasing; (2) essay plan; and (3) final essay. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Supplementary assessment is not available in this unit.
PWAY0003.contactHours:
2h x 14 weeks = 28 hours
8 hours of assessment preparation and self-study = 8 hrs x 14 = 112 hours
APPROX Total: 140 hours

PWAY0004.description: This unit is designed to enhance students' proficiency in both oral and written communication across diverse academic settings. The unit focuses on improving English language skills while also emphasising collaborative teamwork and the preparation of formal reports. Additionally, the unit aims to deepen students' understanding of English language mechanics, such as structure, form, and function, and to develop their ability to apply these concepts effectively.
PWAY0004.outcomes: Students are able to (1) apply appropriate written and oral communication skills; (2) demonstrate competence in English communication skills for academic reading, writing, speaking, and listening; (3) create academic documents as a communication tool; and (4) participate effectively in team projects demonstrating interpersonal and collaborative learning.
PWAY0004.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) team research and individual reflection; (2) interim report - individual; and (3) final report - individual. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Supplementary assessment is not available in this unit.
PWAY0004.contactHours:
2h x 14 weeks = 28 hours
8 hours of assessment preparation and self-study = 8 hrs x 14 = 112 hours
APPROX Total: 140 hours

PWAY0005.description: This unit provides students with an introduction to key mathematical concepts used in everyday life and the workplace. Designed for students with limited mathematical backgrounds, it develops confidence and competence in numeracy, algebra, financial mathematics, measurement and statistics. Students will work individually and collaboratively to complete exercises in each of the content areas. Emphasis is placed on applying mathematical skills to solve practical problems and interpreting results in real-world contexts.
PWAY0005.outcomes: Students are able to (1) apply numerical skills to solve problems involving percentages, ratios and rates in real-world contexts.; (2) simplify algebraic expressions, solve linear equations, rearrange formulas and sketch linear graphs.; (3) perform financial calculations involving wages, taxation, simple and compound interest, and interpret their application in personal and business contexts.; and (4) summarise and interpret data using appropriate statistical measures and apply measurement and geometric principles to solve practical problems..
PWAY0005.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) in class tests and (2) final exam. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.
PWAY0005.contactHours:
2 x 1h lectures x 14 weeks = 28 hours
2h tutorial x 14 weeks = 28 hours
7 hours of assessment preparation and self-study per week = 7 hrs x 14 = 98 hours
APPROX Total = 154 hours

PWAY0006.description: This unit introduces communication skills essential for success in both academic study and future nursing practice. Students will learn strategies for effective interpersonal and collaborative communication within academic and healthcare contexts, including interactions with patients and their families. Emphasis is placed on active listening, cultural safety, basic academic writing, and personal reflection. Through practical and engaging activities and guided reflection, students will build confidence and competence in communicating respectfully, clearly, and professionally, preparing them for further study and professional clinical environments.
PWAY0006.outcomes: Students are able to (1) demonstrate effective oral and written communication skills relevant to academic and healthcare-related contexts; (2) participate in activities that apply appropriate communication strategies, including active listening, empathy, and culturally safe practices.; (3) produce clear and structured written texts using appropriate academic and professional conventions.; and (4) reflect on personal learning and communication development through reflective writing and self-evaluation..
PWAY0006.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) professional writing; (2) role play; and (3) individual presentation and reflection. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Supplementary assessment is not available in this unit.
PWAY0006.contactHours:
2h x 14 weeks = 28 hours
8 hours of assessment preparation and self-study = 8 hrs x 14 = 112 hours
APPROX. Total: 140 hours

PWAY0007.description: This unit develops foundational academic skills in both information literacy and academic writing to support university-level study. Students will learn how to analyse academic tasks, identify information needs, and locate and evaluate credible sources using a range of tools including library databases and the internet. The unit also focuses on integrating research into writing through paraphrasing, quoting, and summarising, while applying appropriate referencing conventions. Emphasis is placed on the full writing process, from planning and researching to drafting, revising, and editing, to produce clear, well-structured academic texts across various formats and purposes.
PWAY0007.outcomes: Students are able to (1) analyse academic tasks to determine key concepts, information needs, and apply appropriate research strategies to locate and evaluate literature related to the health and science contexts; (2) critically appraise the research literature to develop a scientific argument in a health-related topic; (3) integrate source material into writing using paraphrasing, quoting, and summarising, with accurate referencing; and (4) apply academic writing conventions to produce organised, cohesive texts for a range of academic purposes, demonstrating competence in the full writing process.
PWAY0007.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) paraphrasing; (2) annotated bibliography; and (3) literature review. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Supplementary assessment is not available in this unit.
PWAY0007.contactHours:
2h x 14 weeks = 28 hours
9 hours of assessment preparation and self-study = 9 hrs x 14 = 126 hours
APPROX Total: 154 hours

PWAY0008.description: This unit is designed to introduce prospective nursing and STEM students to the structure and function of the human body. Key areas of study include fundamental chemistry, essential biological terminology, cellular function and metabolism, body systems, and the concept of homeostasis. Students will build a broad foundational knowledge while also developing skills in note-taking and relevant mathematical applications. The unit also provides an opportunity for students to reflect on their vocational goal of entering the nursing or science disciplines and to become familiar with the core terminology essential for undergraduate studies.
PWAY0008.outcomes: Students are able to (1) demonstrate an understanding of basic chemistry and biological terminology as they relate to human anatomy and physiology; (2) identify and describe the structure and function of major body systems, including their role in maintaining homeostasis; (3) explain the levels of organisation within the human body and accurately label key anatomical structures; and (4) use appropriate scientific language to communicate foundational concepts in human biology.
PWAY0008.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) topic tests; (2) case study; and (3) final exam. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.
PWAY0008.contactHours:
2 x 1 hour lectures x 14 weeks = 28 hours
2h tutorial x 14 weeks = 28 hours
7 hours of assessment preparation and self-study x 14 = 98 hours
APPROX Total = 154 hours

PWAY0009.description: This unit develops the algebraic and trigonometric skills needed for success in university-level mathematics. Students explore key pre-calculus topics with a focus on developing a strong understanding of mathematical functions and their graphs. Emphasis is placed on problem solving, reasoning, and the use of mathematical representations.
PWAY0009.outcomes: Students are able to (1) apply the laws of indices and algebraic techniques to simplify and factorise expressions, and to solve equations involving linear, quadratic and exponential relationships; (2) interpret and use function notation to describe and graph a range of functions, including linear, quadratic and exponential functions; (3) solve contextual mathematical problems by applying appropriate algebraic methods, demonstrating logical reasoning and clear communication of working; and (4) apply trigonometric concepts and techniques, including the use of radian measure and the unit circle, to solve geometric and real-world problems.
PWAY0009.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) in-class tests and (2) final exam. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.
PWAY0009.contactHours:
2 x 1 hour lectures x 14 weeks = 28 hours
2 hour tutorial x 14 weeks = 28 hours
7 hours x 14 = 98 hours
APPROX: Total: 154 hours

PWAY0010.description: This unit provides students with a foundational understanding of chemical principles and quantitative skills essential for success in university-level Chemistry. Emphasis is placed on conceptual understanding, problem solving and scientific communication within theoretical and applied contexts. The unit includes a theoretical laboratory component focusing on safe practices, correct equipment use and data processing.
PWAY0010.outcomes: Students are able to (1) explain and apply fundamental principles of chemistry to describe and predict the structure and properties of elements and compounds; (2) solve quantitative chemical problems involving chemical equations, the mole concept, gases and solutions; (3) describe and interpret patterns of chemical behaviour using models such as collision theory and the kinetic theory of gases; and (4) demonstrate a theoretical understanding of laboratory practices by describing safe procedures, correct equipment use and measurement uncertainty.
PWAY0010.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: (1) weekly online quizzes; (2) in class tests ; and (3) final exam. Further information is available in the unit outline.



Student may be offered supplementary assessment in this unit if they meet the eligibility criteria.
